tools.name: get_offer
tools.description: What FindingLeads does for a home-service business (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, restoration), who it is for, and the next step. Read this before describing the service to anyone.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: How FindingLeads is priced: the free trial, how monthly plans work, and every one-time done-for-you setup (Google Business Profile, Local Services Ads, reviews, Pro Site, speed-to-lead and more) with its public price and page.

tools.name: estimate_missed_call_cost
tools.description: What unanswered calls cost a home-service business per month, in extra jobs and in dollars, for a given trade and monthly call volume. Returns a band, not a point estimate. Without a real call volume it returns unquantified rather than inventing one.

tools.name: list_trades
tools.description: The home-service trades FindingLeads serves, each with the typical value of one booked job, whether an inbound call is a repair or a project, and how often calls go unanswered in that trade.

tools.name: how_to_fix
tools.description: For one common reason a contractor loses jobs (missed calls, slow follow-up, few reviews, not showing up on Google or AI search, no website): why it costs jobs and what FindingLeads does about it, with the page to start on.

tools.name: google_business_profile_checklist
tools.description: The steps to get a local service business found on Google: Business Profile claim, verification and build-out, Local Services Ads and the Google Guaranteed badge, consistent directory listings, and a review system. Usable as a do-it-yourself checklist; each part also names the done-for-you setup and

tools.name: get_pro_site
tools.description: What a FindingLeads Pro Site is (a contractor website built to turn a visitor into a booked call), the pages it has, what the owner edits versus what stays fixed, what it costs, and where to start one.

tools.name: pro_site_start_link
tools.description: The link that starts a FindingLeads Pro Site draft, with the business name, trade and city filled in when given. The user enters their own email on the page; never ask for it in the chat.

tools.name: pro_site_custom_domain
tools.description: How a contractor puts their Pro Site on a domain they own, what changes for search when they do, and what happens if they keep the directory address instead.

tools.name: list_free_checks
tools.description: The free checks a contractor can run on findingleads.com: the 60-second website audit, the missing-leads count for their trade and area, and the Google opportunity scan. Returns what each one answers and the link to run it. Each check is run by the user on the site, which emails them the report.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_pricing, how_to_fix, google_business_profile_checklist, list_free_checks · Public sink: pro_site_start_link · Destructive: list_free_checks.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_pricing, how_to_fix, google_business_profile_checklist, list_free_checks · Public sink: pro_site_start_link · Destructive: list_free_checks

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_offer" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "What FindingLeads does for a home-service pro, what it costs to start, and the next step. Read this before describing the service to anyone." → after: "What FindingLeads does for a home-service business (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, restoration), who it is for, and the next step. Read this before describing the service to anyone."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
